subject: Gila monster
title: A Lizard's Spit Became a Diabetes Drug Taken by Millions

scenes.text: A lizard's venom led to a drug millions of people take.
In 1992, a doctor in the Bronx found a hormone called exendin-4 in the saliva of the Gila monster.
It copies a gut hormone that tells the body to release insulin when blood sugar is high.
The drug made from it, exenatide, was approved in 2005. It has been prescribed to millions of people.
A slow desert lizard that bites and hangs on. Its spit changed medicine.
